about.title: Rancho Palos Verdes Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death happens because of someone else's carelessness — whether on Palos Verdes Drive S, Hawthorne Boulevard, or somewhere else in the city — the people left behind often face grief alongside confusing legal questions. Los Angeles County's public crash data for Rancho Palos Verdes shows relatively few reported traffic fatalities in recent years, which means fatal incidents here are often tied to other causes: falls, medical negligence, defective products, or workplace accidents on the Peninsula's hillside properties and commercial sites. Whatever the cause, California law gives certain surviving family members a path to hold the responsible party accountable through a civil wrongful death claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise outcomes; we simply help connect families with an independent, contingency-based attorney who can review what happened and explain the options, without adding cost or pressure during an already difficult time.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing mainly to a spouse, domestic partner, or children, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain situations. An attorney can help sort out who in your family has the right to bring the claim.

items.title: A Firm Deadline That Doesn't Wait
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks considerably if a government entity is involved. Getting guidance early helps protect your family's ability to pursue the claim at all.

items.title: No Fee Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to have your case reviewed. You only owe attorney fees if the case results in a recovery.

items.question: What losses can my family recover in a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: California allows recovery for things like funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. It's a civil matter separate from any criminal charges that might arise from the same incident. An attorney can walk you through which losses apply to your specific circumstances.

items.question: Rancho Palos Verdes doesn't report many traffic fatalities — does that mean wrongful death claims are rare here?
items.answer: Traffic deaths reported for the city have been low in recent data, but wrongful death claims can arise from many other situations, including falls, medical errors, or hazardous property conditions common in a hillside community like this one. The absence of a traffic fatality doesn't mean a preventable death claim isn't valid. An attorney can help evaluate the specific facts of your loss.

items.question: How long do we have to file, and does it matter who caused the death?
items.answer: Generally, California gives surviving family two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government agency involve much shorter notice periods. Whether the responsible party was a driver, a property owner, or another entity can affect the process, so it helps to have someone review the details soon rather than later.
